questions.question_text:
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Term } (n) & \text{Lump Sum Factor } (1.005)^n & \text{Annuity FV Factor } (0.5\%) \\ \hline 120 & 1.8194 & 163.8793 \\ 240 & 3.3102 & 462.0409 \\ \hline \end{array}$

Liam contributes to superannuation over $20$ years ($240$ months) at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($0.5\%$ per month). For the first $10$ years ($120$ months), he deposits $\$400$ per month. For the next $10$ years ($120$ months), he increases his monthly deposit to $\$800$. The balance from the first $10$ years earns compound interest over the second $10$ years. Using the table of interest factors above, calculate Liam's total superannuation balance after the full $20$ years ($240$ months).

options.why: Added the two 10-year annuity balances without compounding the first balance over the second 10 years.
Calculated the future value as if $\$800$ was contributed monthly for the entire 240 months.
Compounded the first balance for 240 months instead of the remaining 120 months.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Stage 1 FV (first 10 yr)} = 400 \times 163.8793 = \$65\,551.72$
$\text{Compounded Stage 1 Balance} = 65\,551.72 \times 1.8194 = \$119\,264.80$
$\text{Stage 2 FV (second 10 yr)} = 800 \times 163.8793 = \$131\,103.44$
$\text{Total Superannuation Balance} = 119\,264.80 + 131\,103.44$
$=\$250\,368.24$
